💡 Qualified claim
Professor Lovelore explains the word that sizes a claim
Professor Lovelore Literature expert

One claim, three sizes
Small
Buck’s love for Thornton changes nothing.
says too little
Sized
Buck’s love for Thornton slows the change, but it does not stop it.
fits what the chapter shows
Big
Buck’s love for Thornton changes everything.
says too much

The Cremation of Sam McGee
Robert W. Service (1907) · from “The Cremation of Sam McGee,” stanzas 14 and 15
The speaker opens the boiler door.
· · ·
And there sat Sam, looking cool and calm, in the heart of the furnace roar; And he wore a smile you could see a mile, and he said: "Please close that door. It's fine in here, but I greatly fear you'll let in the cold and storm— Since I left Plumtree, down in Tennessee, it's the first time I've been warm." There are strange things done in the midnight sun By the men who moil for gold; The Arctic trails have their secret tales That would make your blood run cold; The Northern Lights have seen queer sights, But the queerest they ever did see Was that night on the marge of Lake Lebarge I cremated Sam McGee.
· · ·
the heart of the furnace roar: the middle of the roaring fire · Plumtree: Sam’s hometown, as the poem names it · cool and calm: relaxed, not upset at all

ASSAYED
DAWSON ASSAY OFFICE · 1898
Counterclaim: what would a reader on the other side say?
Response: your answer, with a detail from the chapter
My thesis, assayed
Qualifiers: most · partly · for now · only · in one way
Priya · 7th Grade Scholar
Her certificate, as a model

Counterclaim: Some readers would say Buck’s love for Thornton proves the old Buck survives.

Response: But London says that because of that love “he could not steal from this man,” while from every other man he steals without a pause (London, Ch. 6). The love belongs to one man, not to the dog he used to be.

My thesis, assayed (qualifier: most): The North keeps Buck alive, but it destroys most of the fair and trusting dog he was at Judge Miller’s place.

  • You passed the assayer’s test.
  • You chose the heaviest poke against your thesis.
  • You wrote a counterclaim and a response.
  • You kept your thesis or added a qualifier, and wrote the final version.

Three lenses for your introduction
  1. Hook. A reader would want the second sentence.
  2. Thesis. Your claim is the last sentence, and it is the right size for your evidence.
  3. Marks. Every comma that joins two sentences has a joining word.
